topics.topic: Define attempt and NodeExecution identity for the unrecorded and recovery executions
questions: Does the unrecorded execution consume an `attempt_number`, so that the recovery execution's NodeExecution is the next attempt, or is the recovery execution assigned the same first available attempt number?
Does the recordless function execution consume an `attempt_number`, and is the recovery execution the same attempt or a further attempt?
Does the recovery execution retain the unrecorded execution's `attempt_number`, or is it a new attempt with a new `attempt_number` and therefore a different NodeExecution value?

quotes:
For one run, node and element, `attempt_number` is the ordinal of the
   element's NodeExecution M23 records: each NodeExecution written for the
   element takes the next number, from 1, whatever its status — an execution, a
   send, a pre-send failure, an owner's refusal, a skip, an upstream failure, the
   record of a mapped node over an empty list. An EffectAttempt M26 carries the
   number of the NodeExecution that will conclude its send, which is the next
   number when it is written, and an EffectApproval M24 the next number when it
   is requested — the attempt it was requested for — without taking it. Nothing
   else takes or holds a number: waiting for approval writes no NodeExecution,
   and the owner's resolution of an unknown outcome writes no NodeExecution
   (rule 3).

Their bytes are
   removed at once only by a spool-ceiling refusal (A15 rule 3); after any
   other failure they stay in the run's spool, counted toward
   `spool_run_bytes_max`, until that spool is removed (A18 rule 4) or a later
   write to the same position replaces them — a position being the run, node,
   `map_index`, attempt number, port and list index, which only a retry of
   the same attempt number writes again, after a restart left that attempt
   without a record.
judgement.why: State 2 says attempt numbers are ordinals of written NodeExecution records, nothing else takes a number, and restart retries the same unrecorded attempt number.

topics.topic: Define the Run status and lifecycle state between trace-record refusal and recovery
questions: What status does the Run have after the kernel stops and before recovery, and is that status final or resumable?

What Run status and waiting facts apply between the kernel stopping and recovery, given that `pending` is defined only for an unreachable service or unknown outcome and WaitingPoint has no trace-store-refusal reason?
What Run status and lifecycle transition represent the interval after the kernel stops because the trace store refused the record and before recovery executes the function again?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P5 about the Run and WaitingPoint lifecycle between trace-record refusal and startup recovery, on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Run and WaitingPoint lifecycle state between trace-record refusal and recovery
quotes:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
precedent.why: State 2 makes startup recovery derive the existing Run's status and WaitingPoints from durable records and automatically advance it when that derivation is running.

topics.topic: Define which K-09 execution is effective and how outputs and external effects are treated
questions: Which execution has no effect: the unrecorded execution, the recovery execution, or only the duplicate execution as a whole; and are outputs and external effects from the unrecorded execution discarded?
Which execution has no effect: the recordless execution interrupted by the refusal, the recovery execution, or both; and which execution's outputs or effects belong to the run?
Which execution has no effect: the unrecorded execution during which the kernel stopped, or the function execution performed during recovery?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P1 about retained outputs, effects, and model mutations from the unrecorded execution, on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Atomicity and persistence of outputs, external effects, and model mutations from an unrecorded execution
quotes:
An element that does not
      succeed keeps no output: its NodeExecution names none, a value it produced
   is not stored, and the files its attempt spooled are discarded: no
   SpooledFile record names them and nothing reads them.

Their bytes are
   removed at once only by a spool-ceiling refusal (A15 rule 3); after any
   other failure they stay in the run's spool, counted toward
   `spool_run_bytes_max`, until that spool is removed (A18 rule 4) or a later
   write to the same position replaces them — a position being the run, node,
   `map_index`, attempt number, port and list index, which only a retry of
   the same attempt number writes again, after a restart left that attempt
   without a record. Value bytes it published stay in the content-addressed area
   unnamed, reused by equal bytes until the next start removes them (A18 rule
   4); nothing reads either.

function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
precedent.why: State 2 specifies that unrecorded output records are absent, any residual bytes are unreadable and cleaned or replaced, and re-execution is safe because a function has no effect.
